findings.title: The overwrite guard is wired to a function `sq review code` never calls
findings.description: T12/T13 scope the archive-on-overwrite guard to `save_review_file`, and T13's tests exercise that function directly. But `sq review code <N>` — the command named in success criterion 7 (slice design:364) and walkthrough step 7 — persists via `save_review_result` (`src/squadron/cli/commands/review.py:746`), which writes with `path.write_text` directly (`src/squadron/review/persistence.py#save_review_result`). `save_review_file` is reached only from `pipeline/actions/review.py:272`, in the no-`slice_info` fallback. So T12, T13 and their commit can all pass while re-running `sq review code` still destroys hand-written review content; criterion 10 (failed/unverifiable archive aborts the overwrite, original byte-identical) is likewise unmet on that path. No task routes `save_review_result` (or its `as_json` branch) through a shared archive helper, and no test drives the CLI path — T40's walkthrough would only discover the gap at closeout. A task must cover the `save_review_result` writer before Part D lands.

findings.title: Derivation wiring omitted: no mapping to the resolution vocabulary, no `judge_failed`, no disputed outcomes for `--no-judge`
findings.description: T27 says to reuse `derive_addressed_verdict` "verbatim" for the final `resolution`, but that function returns `Verdict.PASS|FAIL|UNKNOWN` (`src/squadron/pipeline/actions/findings_addressed/verification.py:113`), while Decision 5, the Data Flow and the artifact schema require `ADDRESSED|UNADDRESSED|UNKNOWN`. No task defines that translation (T29's `render_resolution` just receives a `resolution` value). Worse, 305's policy explicitly passes `judge_failed=judge.failed` (`policy.py:76`), but T25 asserts transport failure "falls out of the existing behavior … not to add new logic": `JudgeLegResult(failed=True, outcomes=[])` with the default `judge_failed=False` derives PASS → ADDRESSED. The same applies to `--no-judge`, where T25 says residue "stays disputed" but no task materializes those `disputed` outcomes (`statuses_to_outcomes` is fed by a judge response that never happens), so an empty outcome list derives PASS. Criteria 2, 3, 4 and 9 depend on this wiring. T26/T28's tests would catch the wrong result, but the implementation instructions actively steer the implementer away from the fix; state the mapping, the `judge_failed` threading, and the `--no-judge` disputed-outcome construction explicitly.

findings.title: T5/T6 demand unchanged 305 tests but the extraction moves the symbol those tests patch
findings.description: T5 moves the `run_review_with_profile` call into `review/addressed/judge.py`; T6 requires `test_findings_addressed_judge.py` and `test_findings_addressed_e2e.py` to pass unchanged and explicitly says "Confirm no test needed rewriting to pass". Both files patch the string target `squadron.pipeline.actions.findings_addressed.judge.run_review_with_profile` (`tests/pipeline/test_findings_addressed_judge.py:32`, `tests/pipeline/test_findings_addressed_e2e.py:27`), which ceases to be a callable attribute once the transport moves. T1's importer sweep (`grep -rln "findings_addressed.models\|findings_addressed import"`) does not match a patch-target string literal, so no task updates it. Success criterion 12 ("305's full test suite passes unchanged — including after the relocation") is therefore unsatisfiable as written. A task must reconcile the patch seam — keep a patchable re-export in the wrapper, or plan the mechanical test-target edits and say explicitly which test changes are allowed.

findings.title: The relocation reintroduces review→pipeline imports and a package-level cycle
findings.description: The design's F002 (slice design:141) moves the context-free core precisely so `review/` never imports `pipeline/actions/` internals. T3 nevertheless keeps `review/addressed/verification.py` importing `RoundDiff` from `pipeline/actions/findings_addressed/screens.py` (and mislabels that direction as "pipeline→review"), T21 tells the new `review/resolution.py` to import `RoundDiff` and `screen_byte_identical` from that same pipeline module, and T7 populates `review/addressed/__init__.py` with `verify_outcomes`/`derive_addressed_verdict`. Result: initializing `review.addressed` runs `__init__` → `verification` → `pipeline.actions.findings_addressed.screens`; importing that package runs its `__init__` → `policy`, which (after T3's importer updates) imports `review.addressed.verification` before it has defined those names. `RoundDiff` is shared vocabulary used by screens, verification, judge and resolution — it belongs in `review/addressed/` — but no task moves it. This risks import errors at T8's full-suite pass and contradicts the stated dependency direction.

findings.title: Only one of the two `reviewedSha` persistence paths is verified
findings.description: Success criterion 1 (slice design:349) requires the stamp "from both the CLI and the pipeline persistence paths". T10 wires both, but T11's integration test is explicitly either/or — "`save_review_result` (or the pipeline review action, whichever is more directly testable)" — and walkthrough step 1 / T40 grep a single review file. `pipeline/actions/review.py:265-272` also builds markdown via `format_review_markdown` + `save_review_file` in the no-`slice_info` branch, which T10 never mentions. No task verifies the pipeline-action path's stamp or that fallback branch; add a test per path (or drive both through one shared helper so a single test proves parity).

findings.title: The "review discovery" half of the metrology criterion has no test task
findings.description: Success criterion 11 (slice design:375) requires both `discover_judge_results` **and** review discovery to return no resolution artifacts, "test against the real glob". T32 covers only `discover_judge_results` (`src/squadron/metrology/discovery.py:46`). The second surface — `resolve_target`'s `reviews_dir.glob(f"{index}-review.*")` at `src/squadron/metrology/capture.py:97` — is never exercised with a resolution artifact in the directory. T40 asks to "cite the test that proves it" for every criterion; there is no test to cite for this half. Add one assertion against the real `resolve_target` glob in T32.

findings.title: T13's commit lands Part D before T14's go/no-go answer is known
findings.description: The design's Phase 5 note (slice design:381) requires the cf `archive/`-scanning verification "sequenced before Part D lands", and Decision 7 says to confirm it "before landing". The breakdown puts T14 after T12/T13, whose `Commit:` marker (`fix: archive prior review content before overwrite, fail closed on archive failure`) is the point Part D lands. The "do not mark T12 done until T14's verification outcome is known" note gates a checkbox, not the commit: in the recursive case T14 mandates changing the archived filename scheme and updating T12/T13 *after* they were committed and marked tested. Move T14 ahead of T12, or hold the Part D commit until after T14, so the marker sits at a verified working point.

findings.title: Part 0's four identical full-suite checkpoints are redundant for a pure relocation
findings.description: The slice is 3/5 with 13 criteria; the breakdown is 40 tasks across two files (305, comparable scope, used 31). Part 0 is four mechanical moves, each followed by a verification task running the *same* findings-addressed suite unchanged (T2, T4, T6), plus a fourth full-project run (T8), and T40 repeats the full suite at closeout. Criterion 12 needs one "305 suite passes unchanged after the relocation" proof, not four. T7 (effort 1/5 `__all__`/docstring edit) is too granular to justify its own dedicated ruff/pyright/full-suite task. Merge T1+T3 into one move pair with one verification, fold T7 into T5/T6, and keep a single full-suite checkpoint — the test-with pattern is preserved while cutting ~3 tasks and three redundant suite runs.

findings.title: All 13 success criteria trace to task pairs, with consistent test-with ordering
findings.description: Cross-reference: criterion 1→T9–T11, 2→T29–T34, 3→T21/T22, 4→T25/T26, 5→T27/T28, 6→T19/T20, 7+10→T12/T13, 8→T23/T24, 9→T25/T26, 11→T32, 12→T2/T4/T6/T8/T40, 13→T31/T32/T34. Nearly all implementation tasks are immediately followed by their test task in both files, and `Commit:` markers are plain lines at tested points (T2, T4, T6, T8, T11, T13; T16–T37, T40), not checkboxes and not only at the end. T14 correctly appears as its own checklist task per the Phase 5 note, and T37–T39 cover slash-command parity, the schema docs and the PM procedure without cf code changes — no scope creep. No load/NFR restatement in the parent design, so no `tests/load/` or CI-gating task is needed here.
